recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not remove Goal.addresses target profiles for FHIR-6216; any future narrowing should be handled as a new Patient Care decision because both FHIR-6216 and later FHIR-40777 support retaining the references.
issue_request: FHIR-6216 was a Published Patient Care DSTU1 change request that questioned the Goal.concern reference list and proposed removing MedicationStatement, NutritionOrder, and ProcedureRequest. The final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution instead renamed Goal.concern to Goal.addresses and changed the short label from "Health issues this goal addresses" to "Issues addressed by this goal".
initial_application: Jira records SVN #6806 as the application. The imported git-svn commit 8bd3bd917d537625fad908b5f0f6277d113b941e, "Goal tracker items", is that revision and changed Goal.concern to Goal.addresses in the Goal spreadsheet and example, preserving the reference list and changing the short label to "Issues addressed by this goal".
additional_context: Goal is active in source/fhir.ini. The current authoritative source/goal/structuredefinition-Goal.xml defines Goal.addresses with the resolved short label and no remaining Goal.concern path. Later Goal.addresses decisions, especially FHIR-40777, revisited whether intervention-like targets should be removed and again resolved not to remove references, instead clarifying the definition to the current context wording.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current build-scope Goal XML already carries the resolved element name and short label, and later applied context supports retaining the broader target-profile list.
